title: A Variational Formulation of the MHD Induction Equation
abstract:
We present a variational formulation of the induction equation in magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) based on Gauss's principle of least constraint. The central result is the Euler--Lagrange equation $\mathbf{Z}_B = -
abla h_m$, where $h_m = \mathbf{A}\cdot\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic helicity density. This reveals that the magnetic helicity gradient $
abla h_m$ acts as the constraint force maintaining the solenoidality of the magnetic field, exactly as the pressure gradient $
abla p$ maintains incompressibility in Taha et al.'s pressure-gradient minimization principle. The magnetic helicity density---which, though gauge-dependent locally, yields a gauge-invariant variational principle---naturally emerges as the Lagrange multiplier enforcing $
abla\cdot\mathbf{B}=0$. At the solution, the field minimizes the norm of the magnetic helicity gradient $\|
abla h_m\|^2$. This establishes a structural analogy: magnetic helicity is to the magnetic field as pressure is to velocity. The variational principle connects to Woltjer's theorem, Taylor relaxation, and the Hamiltonian structure of MHD.
